To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
NGF has a significant effect on the number of neurons that survive and the morphology of those neurons that do survive.
NGF promotes the survival of adult and aged sensory neurons, and increases the number of neurons with a larger diameter and the number of spindle‐shapd neurons.
NGF has a positive influence on the survival of adult mouse sensory neurons, but has no effect on the survival of aged mouse sensory neurons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of NGF in the survival of sensory neurons.
the effect of exogenous NGF on the survival and morphological characteristics of sensory neurons isolated form adult and aged mice.
the effects of exogenously applied NGF on the survival and morphological differentiation of adult and aged mouse dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons in primary cultures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of NGF in the adult and aged mice are similar in that the number of sensory neurons in cultures supplemented with exogenous NGF was greater than those in control cultures.
NGF is not a survival factor for adult sensory neurons.
NGF is essential for the survival of adult sensory neurons, but is not as essential for the survival or differentiation of neurons from aged mice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the survival of sensory neurons from adult mice is dependent upon the presence of endogenous NGF, and that the addition of exogenous NGF to the culture medium does not significantly increase the survival of these neurons.
NGF is an effective neurotrophic substance for sensory neurons, and its effect is not significantly different between adult and aged mice.
NGF is a potent survival factor and that the survival of sensory neurons is more dependent on NGFs than previously believed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of NGF on the survival of adult and aged mouse neurons are concentration‐dependent, and that NGF can enhance neuronal survival in aged mouse sensory neurons in vitro.
NGF can help to preserve sensory neurons in culture.
NGF is a key player in the survival of sensory neurons in the adult and aging mouse.
